adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same root cause: evt.destinationCalendar can be null/empty, so destructuring yields an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar, and subsequent property access (e.g., .integration) triggers a TypeError/null reference. adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts updateEvent: fallback find compares externalId against falsy externalCalendarId, yielding undefined calendarId that Google rejects

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the fallback branch when `externalCalendarId` is falsy now does `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. Because that branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (e.g., `undefined`/`null`), the `find` comparison will almost always fail and return `undefined`, leaving `selectedCalendar` unset. This is a verifiable logic error introduced by the diff and can result in an undefined `calendarId` being used for the Google API call (unless there is an unseen fallback later).

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts deleteEvent: same falsy externalCalendarId find pattern deletes event from wrong (primary) calendar instead of destination calendar

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new deleteEvent calendar selection logic is incorrect when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It does:
```ts
const calendarId = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
In the else-branch `externalCalendarId` is `null/undefined`, so the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined` and will not select the destination calendar, yielding `undefined` and causing fallback behavior (e.g., "primary") rather than deleting from the intended destination calendar. This matches the finding (same pattern also appears in `updateEvent`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleCancelBooking.ts: raw Prisma Credential has no appName, so getCalendar returns undefined and calendar event is never deleted for non-organizer host team bookings

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts, when a calendar credential isn’t found in bookingToDelete.user.credentials, the diff fetches it via prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } }) and then passes that raw Prisma Credential directly into getCalendar(calendarCredential). Elsewhere in this diff (e.g., EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents / updateBookingReferences), when fetching credentials from DB they also fetch app.slug and construct a CredentialWithAppName-like object including appName. That inconsistency suggests getCalendar may rely on appName (not present on the raw Prisma Credential), which could cause getCalendar to return undefined and skip deletion. However, the diff does not show getCalendar’s implementation, so the failure mode cannot be proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: requestReschedule.handler.ts: dropped fallback to bookingToReschedule.user.destinationCalendar, resulting in empty destinationCalendar array and no calendar event creation

adjudication.rationale: In `requestReschedule.handler.ts`, the previous code was `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar` (no `user.destinationCalendar` fallback existed in the shown diff). The change makes it an array-or-empty-array, but the finding’s claim that a user fallback was dropped is not supported by the diff. Also, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` falls back when `destinationCalendar` is null/empty (`length > 0` check), so “no calendar event creation” is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar.d.ts createEvent signature made credentialId required but only GoogleCalendarService updated; other implementations silently ignore the parameter
matched_golden_ids: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the Calendar interface/type now requires a credentialId parameter for createEvent, but not all concrete implementations were updated (e.g., only Google was), causing an interface/contract mismatch across other services.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google CalendarService deleteEvent fallback is dead code: the find predicate compares cal.externalId === externalCalendarId but only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it never matches; legacy bookings without externalCalendarId get undefined calendarId and the delete fails (same pattern duplicated in updateEvent line 256 and deleteEvent line 315)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` compute the calendar id as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` (and similarly in `updateEvent`). When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), so it will almost never match a real calendar externalId, yielding `undefined`. This makes the intended fallback to a destination calendar effectively dead/incorrect code and can lead to using an undefined/incorrect calendarId when `externalCalendarId` isn’t provided.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lark and Office365 CalendarServices only use the first host's calendar (mainHostDestinationCalendar), dropping multi-host support for collective events — the PR's stated purpose — creating the event only on the first host's calendar

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over `event.destinationCalendar` to create events per destination (passing `destination.externalId` via `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`). However, `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` and `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` ignore per-destination selection and instead always destructure only the first entry (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId/eventsUrl = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`). This means when `destinationCalendar` contains multiple hosts (e.g. collective), those services will create events only on the first destination calendar (and potentially duplicate on it for each loop iteration), dropping multi-host support.

adjudication_records.issue_text: requestReschedule.handler.ts drops the user.destinationCalendar fallback, yielding [] instead of falling back to the organizer's calendar like every other converted call site, so reschedule diverges from the booking path

adjudication.rationale: In `requestReschedule.handler.ts` the PR sets `destinationCalendar` to `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule.destinationCalendar] : []`, with no fallback to `bookingToReschedule.user.destinationCalendar` (or equivalent organizer/user fallback) unlike many other updated call sites in this diff (e.g. `confirm.handler.ts`, `editLocation.handler.ts`, payment webhooks) that do `booking.destinationCalendar ? [..] : user.destinationCalendar ? [..] : []`. While the finding's wording "drops" a fallback isn't strictly accurate (the previous code was `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar`), the diff-grounded issue remains: reschedule now diverges from the common fallback behavior and will produce an empty destination calendar array when the booking lacks one.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking only persists evt.destinationCalendar[0] to the booking's singular Prisma destinationCalendar relation, so multi-host calendar state is lost after creation and cancel/reschedule/webhooks reconstruct from only the first calendar

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking, evt.destinationCalendar is now an array (and for COLLECTIVE team events it explicitly pushes additional members’ destination calendars), but the booking persistence still connects only the first element: `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` (apps/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts around the booking create data). Elsewhere in the diff, many places reconstruct `evt.destinationCalendar` from the booking’s singular `booking.destinationCalendar` (wrapping it into a one-element array), e.g. bookingReminder.ts, payments webhooks, confirm/editLocation/cancel handlers. This means any additional destination calendars added to the event are not persisted and cannot be reconstructed from the booking later, losing multi-host calendar state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests verify the new multi-host behavior: no assertions that collective bookings create events on each host's calendar, that credentialId-based calendar selection works, or that DB-fetched credential paths work; the only e2e change updates a mock fixture

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new behavior around multi-destination calendars / multi-host collective handling (e.g., `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and may fetch credentials from DB via `prisma.credential.findUnique`; `CalendarManager.createEvent` now passes `credential.id` into `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` and returns `externalId`/`credentialId`). However, the only visible test change is in `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts`, updating a fixture field from `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []`, with no new assertions validating (1) events are created for each host/calendar in collective mode, (2) credentialId-based calendar selection (Google `find(cal.credentialId === credentialId)`), or (3) the DB-fallback credential fetch paths. This is a concrete missing-test concern tied directly to new nontrivial logic, not a proven runtime defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleCancelBooking DB-fetched credential lacks the app/appName relation required by getCalendar (unlike the parallel EventManager implementation which includes app and maps appName), so canceling a booking referencing a team host's credential may resolve the calendar service incorrectly or throw

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking, both the pre-existing path (finding credential in bookingToDelete.user.credentials) and the new DB fallback (prisma.credential.findUnique without include) yield a plain Prisma Credential without an app/appName mapping. The diff does not show that getCalendar requires an app relation/appName, nor that cancellation previously relied on it. EventManager’s DB fetch includes app/slug because it constructs a CredentialWithAppName for CalendarManager.createEvent, but handleCancelBooking calls getCalendar directly and the diff provides no evidence that missing app/appName would “resolve incorrectly or throw.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts updateEvent/deleteEvent dead logic: else-branch fallback `find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match since externalCalendarId is falsy, dropping the old destinationCalendar.externalId fallback and causing legacy booking updates/deletes to target null/primary instead of the destination calendar

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the fallback calendar ID as:

- `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else-branch case), the `.find(...)` predicate compares `cal.externalId` to that same falsy value, so it will almost never match a real calendar externalId. This drops the prior behavior (using the destination calendar’s externalId) and will likely result in `selectedCalendar/calendarId` being `undefined`, causing operations to fall back to default/primary or fail. The finding correctly points out this dead/incorrect fallback logic introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: requestReschedule.handler.ts drops the user.destinationCalendar fallback that sibling files preserve, so users with only a personal destination calendar get an empty array and lose calendar attribution in the reschedule cancellation email

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts`, `destinationCalendar` is now set to `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar] : []`, with no fallback to `bookingToReschedule?.user?.destinationCalendar` (or similar). Many sibling handlers in the diff explicitly preserve the user fallback (e.g., `confirm.handler.ts`, `editLocation.handler.ts`, `deleteCredential.handler.ts`). This makes the reschedule-cancellation `CalendarEvent` carry an empty `destinationCalendar` array when only the user's personal destination calendar is set, which can break downstream calendar attribution/templating that expects a destination calendar (now an array).

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts loadUsers rewrite removes `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from prisma.user.findMany select for dynamic bookings, causing user.organization.slug to be undefined for consumers

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, the rewritten loadUsers() path for dynamic bookings (when !eventTypeId) still does `select: { ...userSelect.select, credentials: true, metadata: true }` but the previous explicit `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` selection is removed. If downstream code expects `user.organization.slug` to exist (which the prior explicit select strongly suggests), Prisma will not return it unless it is included in `userSelect.select` (not shown in this diff), leading to `undefined` at runtime for consumers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts loadUsers new error handling throws 400 for any PrismaClientKnownRequestError including routine record-not-found, changing semantics from previous fall-through

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `loadUsers` only calls `prisma.user.findMany(...)`, which does not throw a Prisma “record not found” error (it returns an empty array). No `findUniqueOrThrow`/`findFirstOrThrow` is introduced here. While the new `catch` does map any `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` to an HTTP 400, the specific claim about “routine record-not-found” changing semantics from the previous fall-through is not supported by the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:1060-1076 sets destinationCalendar default to null instead of [], so optional-chained ?.push is a no-op when organizer has no destination calendar, dropping collected team calendars in the collective multi-host case

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, the constructed `evt` sets `destinationCalendar` to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`... : null,` around lines ~1040-1067). Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events it does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. If `destinationCalendar` is `null`, this optional-chained push is a no-op, so any `teamDestinationCalendars` collected from other hosts are silently dropped. This is verifiable from the diff and would break the intended collective multi-host destination calendar aggregation; using `[]` instead of `null` would allow pushing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts createEvent sets organizer.email from mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId (first calendar) while selectedCalendar is resolved by credentialId, so the organizer email may belong to a different host than the calendar being written to

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `createEvent`, the calendar being written to is chosen via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` (i.e., per-credential), but the organizer attendee `email` is taken from `mainHostDestinationCalendar` which is destructured as the *first* element of `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar`. When `destinationCalendar` contains multiple entries (now supported elsewhere in the diff, e.g. collective team events pushing multiple calendars), the first calendar may not correspond to the credential-specific `selectedCalendar`, causing the organizer email to not match the calendar actually used for `events.insert`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts other_calendar branch still uses single-reference booking.references.find while the rest was migrated to multi-reference, so collective bookings with other_calendar credentials only update one host's calendar

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.ts, the “other_calendar” update branch still does `booking.references.find((ref) => ref.type === cred.type)` (see the block starting with `.filter((cred) => cred.type.includes("other_calendar")) ... const calendarReference = booking.references.find(...)`). Elsewhere in this diff, `_calendar` references were explicitly migrated to multi-reference handling via `filter(...includes("_calendar"))` and iterating all matches. If a booking can now have multiple references for the same other_calendar integration/type (e.g., collective/multi-host scenarios), this branch would only pick the first matching reference and miss updating others. The diff alone shows the inconsistency, but it doesn’t conclusively prove multiple same-type other_calendar references exist at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Bundled unrelated cosmetic changes (organiser→organizer typo fix, orginalBookingDuration rename) in a PR titled as a collective-destination-calendar fix, indicating scope drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes changes unrelated to the destination-calendar/collective handling refactor, e.g. changing the notes string from "organiser" to "organizer" in `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts` and renaming `orginalBookingDuration` to `originalBookingDuration` in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts`. These are cosmetic/cleanup edits that broaden the PR scope beyond the collective destination calendar fix, which is a valid review concern even if not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts destinationCalendar fallback is dead code: when externalCalendarId is falsy the predicate can never match, so the fallback always evaluates to undefined, causing update/delete calls to hit Google with calendarId: undefined or the wrong calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new fallback logic for `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` in `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` is effectively dead when `externalCalendarId` is falsy: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` can’t match anything meaningful if `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, so it returns `undefined`. Previously it fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`; now it can result in `calendarId` being `undefined` (or not selecting the intended destination calendar), matching the finding’s claim about incorrect/undefined calendar selection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: requestReschedule.handler.ts compares bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar to itself instead of the user's destinationCalendar, losing the fallback so reschedule flows get an empty destinationCalendar

adjudication.rationale: In `requestReschedule.handler.ts`, `destinationCalendar` is now set to `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule.destinationCalendar] : []` (previously it redundantly used `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar`). Unlike many other updated call sites in this diff (e.g. `confirm.handler.ts`, `editLocation.handler.ts`) that fall back to `user.destinationCalendar`, this handler has no fallback and will produce an empty array when the booking has no `destinationCalendar`, which can break reschedule flows that expect a destination calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts merge path deletes only the first calendar reference of the old booking via .find(), leaving secondary hosts' stale duplicated calendar events after a reschedule merge

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.ts, calendar references were refactored from a single reference to an array (using `.filter(...)` and iterating `for (const reference of calendarReference)`), but the merge cleanup path still deletes only one old calendar reference: `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));`. If the old booking had multiple `_calendar` references (e.g., secondary hosts / multiple destination calendars), only the first will be deleted, leaving other stale calendar events after a merge (newBookingId case).

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts: evt.destinationCalendar is now an array but the booking write persists only destinationCalendar[0] with a single connect, so downstream readers only see the first host's calendar

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, evt.destinationCalendar is built as an array (including additional teamDestinationCalendars for COLLECTIVE team events), but the Prisma write still persists only the first element: `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` (near the booking create/update payload). This means the Booking record’s `destinationCalendar` relation will represent only the primary/first calendar even if multiple were used for event creation. The diff also shows downstream update/delete logic has been refactored to rely on multiple `_calendar` references rather than `booking.destinationCalendar`, so this may be intentional, but it is a concrete scope/consistency concern introduced by the array change rather than a definite functional break proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts: when eventType.destinationCalendar and organizerUser.destinationCalendar are both null, evt.destinationCalendar is null and ?.push silently discards all team members' destinationCalendars for collective events

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when both `eventType.destinationCalendar` and `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` are falsy (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Immediately after, for collective team events, the code tries to append team members’ destination calendars via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, the optional chaining makes this a no-op, so collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently dropped. This is exactly the scenario described in the finding and is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:100-122: organizer email is set from the first destinationCalendar's externalId which may belong to a different host's account than the credential-matched target calendar, causing Google to reject or misattribute events

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `createEvent`, the target `calendarId` is chosen by matching `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, but the organizer attendee email is derived from the *first* destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ...; email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? ... : organizer.email`). With `destinationCalendar` now an array (and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` loops over multiple destinations/credentials), this can set the organizer attendee email to a different host's destination calendar than the credential-matched calendar being inserted into, causing incorrect payload attribution and potential Google API rejection/misbehavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts update path: when a credential is missing, updateEvent(credential, ...) still called and getCalendar(undefined) throws, causing one broken credential to cascade into failing updates for all other references in the loop
loadUsers in handleNewBooking.ts silently dropped organization: { select: { slug: true } } from the user select, breaking org slug resolution for dynamic/username-based booking links

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, the prisma.user.findMany() branch inside loadUsers (when !eventTypeId) previously selected organization: { select: { slug: true } }, but in the diff that selection is removed (now only ...userSelect.select, credentials: true, metadata: true). The diff alone verifies the field was dropped, but it does not show any subsequent usage that definitively proves org slug resolution is now broken (userSelect.select might already include organization, or org slug might not be needed in this path).

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback logic in CalendarService.ts searches for a calendar whose externalId equals a falsy externalCalendarId, so the fallback never matches and evaluates to undefined, causing updates/deletes to target the wrong calendar

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` set the fallback calendar ID like:
- `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`
- `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`
When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the condition that triggers the fallback), the `find` compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), which will not match any real externalId and yields `undefined`. This makes the fallback ineffective and can cause updates/deletes to default elsewhere (e.g., primary) rather than the intended destination calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts accesses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without null-checking, throwing a TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or empty

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the new array-based handling does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` in `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`, so accessing `.integration` will throw a `TypeError`. The diff also shows callers can set `destinationCalendar` to `null` (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts` sets it to `... : null`), making this a real reachable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts sets evt.destinationCalendar to null and then uses optional-chain push, silently dropping all team members' destination calendars when the organizer has none

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized as `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [..] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [..] : null` (not `[]`). Immediately after, for collective team events it does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. If the organizer has no destination calendar and `eventType.destinationCalendar` is unset, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, so the optional-chained `push` is a no-op and the collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently dropped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DB write in handleNewBooking.ts persists only evt.destinationCalendar[0].id, so multi-host destination calendars are lost after the initial write for reschedules/cancellations/recurring flows

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and, for COLLECTIVE team events, appends additional team members’ destination calendars (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`). However, the DB write in `handleNewBooking.ts` still persists only a single relation by connecting `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` (Prisma `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`). This means any additional destination calendars added to the event are not stored on the booking record, creating a mismatch between in-memory behavior (multi-destination) and persisted data (single destination). Whether this breaks reschedule/cancel flows cannot be proven from the diff alone (those flows may rely on calendar references instead), but the persistence is definitively incomplete relative to the new array semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated cosmetic inversion of IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED logic in create.handler.ts bundled into an unrelated PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes a change in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts` that flips the conditions around `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` for setting `slug` and `metadata.requestedSlug` (from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` / `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })` to ternaries). This is unrelated to the primary PR theme (destinationCalendar becoming an array / calendar event handling) and is a scope/PR-hygiene concern. Whether the inversion is correct or a bug can’t be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated user-facing string change 'hidden by the organiser' to 'hidden by the organizer' in CalendarManager.ts bundled into this PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts` changes a user-facing string when `calEvent.hideCalendarNotes` is true from "Notes have been hidden by the organiser" to "Notes have been hidden by the organizer". This is verifiably present and is unrelated to the broader refactor in this PR (destinationCalendar becoming an array, credential/calendar selection logic), so it’s a scope/consistency concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts createAllCalendarEvents: credential fetched by ID without ownership/tenant check, bypassing previous calendarCredentials scoping (broken object-level authorization)

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.ts `createAllCalendarEvents`, when a `destination.credentialId` is not found in `this.calendarCredentials`, the new code falls back to `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })` and then uses that credential to `createEvent(...)`. This fetch is done solely by ID with no `userId`/`teamId`/org scoping or ownership check, which can bypass the previous restriction to `this.calendarCredentials` and is a concrete object-level authorization risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleCancelBooking.ts: credential lookup by reference.credentialId with no userId/org filter, allowing deletion of calendar events using another user's OAuth credential

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts, when a calendar credential isn’t found on bookingToDelete.user.credentials, the new fallback fetches it directly from the DB via prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } }) and then uses it to delete calendar events (getCalendar(calendarCredential) -> calendar?.deleteEvent(...)). This lookup has no additional constraint (e.g., userId/teamId/org) tying the credential to the booking’s user, so a booking reference containing another user’s credentialId could cause the server to operate using that other OAuth credential.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts updateAllCalendarEvents fallback: updateEvent called with credential undefined when credentialFromDB is null, causing crash on credential.id/key dereference
matched_golden_ids: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying bug: when a credential ID exists but the credential lookup returns null/not found, updateEvent is still invoked with an undefined credential, leading to a runtime crash from dereferencing credential fields.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateAllCalendarEvents DB-fallback credential lookup by bare reference.credentialId lacks ownership scoping, allowing updates with arbitrary tenant's credential

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager’s calendar update path, when a matching in-memory credential isn’t found it now falls back to `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: reference.credentialId } })` (and similarly in `createAllCalendarEvents` for `destination.credentialId`). This lookup is only by raw `credentialId` with no scoping/authorization check (e.g., `userId`, `teamId`, org), so if a booking/reference can be influenced to contain an arbitrary `credentialId`, the code would load and use another tenant’s credential to update/create/delete calendar events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent/deleteEvent: dead-code .find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) in falsy-externalCalendarId branches always yields undefined

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`, `selectedCalendar/calendarId` is computed as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined (the else branch), the `.find(...)` predicate compares to `undefined`, so it will always return `undefined` and cannot select a destination calendar. This is a regression from the prior logic (`: event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) and can lead to passing an undefined calendar id to the Google API (or at least failing to target the intended destination calendar).

adjudication_records.issue_text: log.error('createEvent failed', ...) logs full calendar events including attendee emails and notes

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts`, the error handler for calendar creation logs the entire `calEvent` object: `log.error("createEvent failed", JSON.stringify(error), calEvent);`. `CalendarEvent` (per `packages/types/Calendar.d.ts`) includes `attendees` (with emails) and fields like `additionalNotes`/notes-related content, so this log statement can emit PII/sensitive data to logs on failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The only test change is a tautological snapshot update (destinationCalendar: null → []) that mirrors the new sentinel value without verifying collective bookings create events on every host's destination calendar; the PR's headline feature (multi-host fan-out, DB credential fetch fallback, per-credential calendar selection) has zero assertions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior (e.g., destinationCalendar becomes an array; EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now loops/fans out over multiple destination calendars and may fetch missing credentials from DB; GoogleCalendarService.createEvent now selects calendar per credentialId). However, the only test change shown is in `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts`, updating `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []`, which simply aligns with the new sentinel/shape and does not assert the new multi-host fan-out / per-credential selection / DB fallback behavior. This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in coverage rather than a demonstrated runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code in CalendarService.ts updateEvent/deleteEvent: the fallback branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, but the find predicate compares cal.externalId === externalCalendarId which can never match, so it always yields undefined; the previous fallback to event.destinationCalendar?.externalId was silently dropped, meaning update/delete with no external ID now targets undefined calendarId.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` changed the fallback calendar selection from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. This fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, which will not match any real calendar externalId and yields `undefined`. As a result, `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` can become `undefined` and the Google API call targets an undefined calendarId (previously it would use the event's destination calendar).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:117 dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without a null guard; since evt.destinationCalendar can now be [], mainHostDestinationCalendar can be undefined and .integration throws, whereas the old optional-chain version was null-safe.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the new code sets `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then does `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without optional chaining or a falsy check. Since `evt.destinationCalendar` can be `[]` (many call sites in the diff now pass `[]` when no destination calendar), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` can be `undefined`, making `.integration` throw at runtime. The prior code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which was null-safe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:1000-1003 pushes teamDestinationCalendars into evt.destinationCalendar with no test asserting that a collective booking with N hosts produces N calendar events on the correct host calendars; if evt.destinationCalendar was null the push is a no-op and no test would fail.

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, evt.destinationCalendar is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events it does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`, which becomes a no-op when it’s null. That means team members’ `destinationCalendar`s collected into `teamDestinationCalendars` will be silently dropped in that case, so downstream logic (e.g., EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents only iterates when `destinationCalendar.length > 0`) won’t create per-host calendar events. The finding’s note about missing test is secondary, but the null + optional-chaining push behavior is a real correctness issue visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New DB-fetch fallback branches in EventManager.ts and handleCancelBooking.ts silently skip the reference when the credential is still not found (no error result pushed, unlike the previous success: false path), potentially orphaning calendar events after a cancel, and no test triggers this miss path.

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts, when a calendar reference has credentialId but that credential is neither in bookingToDelete.user.credentials nor found via the new prisma.credential.findUnique fallback, the code simply does nothing for that reference (no delete attempt, no fallback to iterating other calendar credentials, no logged/returned failure), leaving the external calendar event potentially undeleted/orphaned. This is visible in the new loop: it only proceeds inside `if (calendarCredential) { ... }` and has no else branch for the “still not found” case. A similar silent-skip pattern exists in EventManager.ts createAllCalendarEvents: destinations with credentialId are ignored if the credential still isn’t found after DB lookup (`if (credential) { createEvent... }` with no else/error result), so missing-credential destinations don’t produce a failure result. The diff also adds no tests covering this miss path (only adjusts an existing e2e expectation for destinationCalendar).
